The ironic reply to their own vow-language follows, telling them to keep the vows they swore to the queen of the sky, כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָֽה צְבָאוֹת֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֵאמֹ֗ר אַתֶּ֨ם וּנְשֵׁיכֶ֜ם וַתְּדַבֵּ֣רְנָה בְּפִיכֶם֮ וּבִידֵיכֶ֣ם מִלֵּאתֶ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ עָשֹׂ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה אֶת נְדָרֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָדַ֨רְנוּ֙ לְקַטֵּר֙ לִמְלֶ֣כֶת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְהַסֵּ֥ךְ לָ֖הּ נְסָכִ֑ים הָקֵ֤ים תָּקִ֨ימְנָה֙ אֶת נִדְרֵיכֶ֔ם וְעָשֹׂ֥ה תַעֲשֶׂ֖ינָה אֶת נִדְרֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.44.25, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says, 'You and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and with your hands have fulfilled it, saying, "We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to her." "'Establish then your vows, and perform your vows.'” (web:Jer.44.25) -- WEB's own layout marks a paragraph fold inside this verse (tier-4 metadata, not evidence for or against a boundary); a petuchah closes oshb:Jer.44.25 (the Prophets-addendum ruling caps it at tier-3, weak, on WLC's single-witness record). The oath proper reopens on lakhen shim'u devar YHWH, echoing this span's own opening imperative rather than a fresh narrative tag reintroducing the speaker, לָכֵן֙ שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֔ה כָּל יְהוּדָ֕ה הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הִנְנִ֨י נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתִּי בִּשְׁמִ֤י הַגָּדוֹל֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם יִהְיֶה֩ ע֨וֹד שְׁמִ֜י נִקְרָ֣א בְּפִ֣י כָּל אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֹמֵ֛ר חַי אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה בְּכָל אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.44.26, byte), matching “Therefore hear Yahweh's word, all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt: 'Behold, I have sworn by my great name,' says Yahweh, 'that my name will no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, "” (web:Jer.44.26) the formula Judah's own men will no longer be able to swear is quoted next, “As the Lord Yahweh lives."” (web:Jer.44.26) the divine title's qamats-pointed form (one of 11 divine-title adonai sites, sweep: 11 of 13 verses, point-aware against the two courtly hiriq sites addressed to Zedekiah elsewhere in the book); four paseq segs stand across this span -- one at oshb:Jer.44.25, two here at oshb:Jer.44.26, and one at oshb:Jer.44.30 — four segs total, from the single-witness seg layer; the tally gives a count, not a position within any verse. The negative and positive halves of the sentence follow without a break, הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁקֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם לְרָעָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א לְטוֹבָ֑ה וְתַמּוּ֩ כָל אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּחֶ֥רֶב וּבָרָעָ֖ב עַד כְּלוֹתָֽם (oshb:Jer.44.27, byte), matching “Behold, I watch over them for evil, and not for good; and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until they are all gone.” (web:Jer.44.27) and וּפְלִיטֵ֨י חֶ֜רֶב יְשֻׁב֨וּן מִן אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָ֖ה מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֑ר וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כָּל שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה הַבָּאִ֤ים לְאֶֽרֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם דְּבַר מִ֥י יָק֖וּם מִמֶּ֥נִּי וּמֵהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.44.28, byte), matching “Those who escape the sword will return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah few in number. current_row.boundary_rationale: A setumah closes oshb:Jer.46.26 in the parashah inventory (WLC, single-witness disclosure: weak, tier-3, serving as Prophets-addendum corroboration). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own opening address to Jacob, distinct in both addressee and content from the judgment just closed, וְ֠אַתָּה אַל תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ וְאַל תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲק֛וֹב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד (oshb:Jer.46.27, byte), matching “But don’t you be afraid, Jacob my servant.
